"Green: variation ≤25 cents and periodicity ≥0.90. Yellow: up to 60 cents, periodicity 0.80–0.90 or no previous neighbor. Orange: greater variation or periodicity <0.80. The weaker endpoint determines the link; stability and periodicity are different measures. Color does not confirm a note. Dashed line: display link between measured endpoints, with no intermediate samples."

"%1$s outside Fitted · %2$s original readings excluded from the trend. Isolated excursions are omitted without emptying the curve; brief uncertain intervals link only nearby measured endpoints. "Orange circles: original estimates, with no confirmed note. Hold at their time to inspect Hz and confidence; use Show all to include those outside the range."

"Bore impedance resonances and emitted harmonics are different quantities. They are not matched by order. The player, temperature and actual geometry affect them; the model is not equivalent to CADSD."
"Number of cycles per second. A higher frequency corresponds to a higher-pitched sound."
"Musical name of a nearby frequency, using A4 = 440 Hz as reference."

"Component near an integer multiple of the fundamental. H2 is near twice its frequency. A candidate is not a confirmation."
"One semitone equals 100 cents. +10 indicates a small deviation toward a higher pitch, without judging instrument quality."
"Higher register played by the performer. A strong drone peak does not imply a register change."

"Logarithmic difference from an analysis reference. This is not absolute sound pressure or calibrated volume."

Chart peaks are sound components. Toots are playing modes that you need to play separately to measure them. The highest peak is not necessarily the fundamental.

Evolutionary search is implemented in Kotlin for this project. It does not use DidgeLab Python code; it uses classical 1D propagation equations, approximate losses and a pitch-based error function.
"The search is reproducible with a fixed seed. Its accuracy must be validated with physical measurements."
"One cent is 1/100 of a semitone. A positive value is higher than the theoretical note."

"The low note produced by your usual lip vibration. For example, D2 ≈ 73.4 Hz."
"Frequencies that make up a note’s timbre. They are different from toots."
"Higher modes played by adjusting your lips. Measure them individually."
"The resistance you feel while playing. A spectrum alone cannot predict that sensation."
Try the PVC preset first, then Conical and Bell. Change one dimension at a time and compare impedance peaks. Results are estimates; measure prototypes to calibrate the model.
"To carve a wooden instrument, start with dry wood, test the bore before gluing and do not use fire indoors."

No Internet access, advertising, accounts or audio uploads. Measure requests microphone permission when starting and saves each session as a private WAV when stopped. Export creates a copy wherever you choose.
The acoustic transmission simulation and evolutionary search are original Kotlin implementations inspired by the public ideas of DidgeLab and CADSD, not their original engines.
